meta.note: Structured view of REPORT.md section 6. REPORT.md holds the reasoning; this file holds the fields an agent needs to filter and cite.

findings.title: Username enumeration via login error code
evidence: POST /api/auth/login returns 404 {error, code:"no_user"} for an unknown handle
A known handle with a bad password returns a different response
Observed in capture har:2
findings.impact: Anyone can test whether a handle is registered. Enables targeted phishing, credential-stuffing shortlists and player-base mapping.
findings.recommendation: Return one generic failure code for both cases and do not echo the submitted username.

findings.title: Client-authoritative economic state on save
findings.severity_note: conditional — high only if the server does not re-validate; unproven
evidence: PUT /api/save accepts the full game object including money, bank, businesses, invest, bets, cars, fleet, ledger, tax, rentOwed
The only integrity control visible is `base`, which detects concurrent edits, not implausible values
Server replies 200 {ok, updatedAt}; nothing in the response indicates a validation pass
findings.impact: If unvalidated: arbitrary currency and asset creation, economy corruption, monetisation bypass.
findings.recommendation: Validate every economic field against server-held authoritative values, or persist deltas only. Reject implausible jumps.
findings.do_not_test_reason: Testing requires writing forged state into a live account. Needs written vendor permission and a staging account.

findings.title: Floating-point currency
evidence: An observed balance carried five decimal places
Monetary values are JSON numbers, not integer minor units
findings.impact: Binary-float drift across interest, fees, rent and tax: off-by-one balances, failed exact comparisons, rounding exploits.
findings.recommendation: Store kobo as integers or as decimal strings.

findings.title: Client-submitted XP in /api/levels
evidence: POST /api/levels body is {op, xp} with xp chosen by the client
Server did not blindly add it: xp moved 16 -> 30 after submitting xp:26
Still client-originated input with unknown validation depth
findings.impact: If weakly validated: level and streak inflation, chest and spin-reward farming.
findings.recommendation: Derive XP from server-recorded actions; accept an action id rather than an amount.

findings.title: admin flag exposed to the client
evidence: GET /api/auth/me returns user.admin as a boolean
findings.impact: No impact by itself. Becomes high if any endpoint trusts a client-supplied or cached admin value.
findings.recommendation: Confirm server-side authorisation on every privileged route; consider omitting the flag from the payload.

findings.title: CSRF posture
evidence: All cookies (ll_session, ll_vid, ll_pass, ll_dev) are HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax
OPTIONS /api/send with a foreign Origin returned 204 with no Access-Control-Allow-Origin
Cross-origin GET /api/auth/me returned no ACAO header
API is JSON-only, so cross-site HTML forms cannot produce a valid request
findings.impact: Cross-site request forgery is not practically exploitable.
findings.recommendation: Add server-side Origin/Sec-Fetch-Site checks so safety is intentional rather than incidental. Make state-changing operations non-GET (see F-12).

findings.title: Verbose, input-echoing error text
evidence: Login error echoes the submitted username
Errors expose internal state such as 'Please log in' and capacity messages
findings.impact: Confirms internal state to an attacker and aids enumeration.
findings.recommendation: Keep friendly UI copy, add stable machine codes, never echo input.

findings.title: Personal data in semi-public listings
evidence: /api/forbes exposes a top-50 leaderboard with profiles
/api/players search returns 25 players per response
/api/verified returns 21 [id, name] pairs
/api/world exposes a live online count (20,475 observed)
findings.impact: Aggregate player enumeration and activity telemetry; combines with F-01 for account mapping.
findings.recommendation: Rate-limit and paginate search; consider hiding exact online counts.

findings.title: Client build-id used as a trust signal
evidence: PUT /api/save includes build: "1792451178"
The client gates behaviour on /api/version and /build.json
findings.impact: A modified client can claim any build id. No security decision should depend on it.
findings.recommendation: Treat the build id as telemetry only.

findings.title: Long-lived session and device cookies
evidence: ll_session expires in about 60 days
ll_dev expires in about 1 year
No evidence of rotation on password change or privilege change
findings.impact: Any cookie exfiltration path yields long-lived authenticated access.
findings.recommendation: Rotate sessions on password change, shorten the idle window with refresh, and document ll_dev's purpose.

findings.title: No __Host- cookie prefix
evidence: Cookies are named ll_session, ll_vid, ll_pass, ll_dev
No __Host- prefix, which would forbid a Domain attribute
findings.impact: A compromised sibling subdomain could plant a cookie with the auth name (cookie tossing / session fixation).
findings.recommendation: Rename to __Host-ll_session etc. and ensure no Domain attribute is set.

findings.title: State-changing operations exposed as GET
evidence: GET /api/wallet/verify?checkout_id= verifies a checkout
GET /api/ads/verify?checkout_id= verifies an ad payment
SameSite=Lax still sends cookies on top-level cross-site navigation
findings.impact: A crafted link can trigger verification for the victim's own pending checkout. Low impact; requires a valid checkout_id.
findings.recommendation: Move verification to POST and reject GET on state-changing routes.
